claims.text: POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for no-show, to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider. The trip record's in_app_calls array is empty and the derived contact_before_cancel block reports call_count of 0, while the platform chat log's three entries include no voice-call entry. The call limb is therefore missing, and the clause provides that if either element is missing the fee is voided and the rider is not charged.

The driver's own statement — 'I sent 2 messages and waited more than 5 minutes. Passenger never reply.' — concedes the position: messages alone are not the obligation. The two messages (MSG-05052-001 at 19:31:30 and MSG-05052-002 at 19:34:10, both before cancelled_at at 19:37:20) satisfy only the first limb of POL-NS-23. The clause is conjunctive and its second limb is unperformed, so the contact obligation is not met and the fee fails.

Even on the driver's best possible version of the timing — arrived_at 19:31:00, free-wait expiry 19:36:00, cancelled_at 19:37:20, elapsed 380.0 seconds — only the free-wait rule in POL-NS-21 is satisfied. POL-NS-21 governs how long the driver must wait; it does not license the charge. POL-NS-23 imposes a separate, cumulative precondition on the very same cancellation, and because that precondition is unmet no no-show fee may be charged at all.

The rider's explanation that he was in a lift with no signal is not corroborated by the record — the chat log shows both driver messages were delivered and read (read_at 19:31:40 and 19:34:23). That does not weaken the claim, and the rider should not have to rely on it: POL-NS-23's contact obligation is unconditional and does not turn on where the rider was or whether he responded. A rider momentarily out of signal is precisely the situation the policy addresses by requiring a call as well as a message, and the entitlement to a refund is independent of the rider's whereabouts.

The rider filed this dispute (filed_by RIDER) and the payments ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 5.00 SGD and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 — nothing has been returned. Under POL-GEN-03 a rider-side filing that is entirely right produces FULL_REFUND of the whole contested amount, and POL-NS-23 fixes the consequence of a voided fee as refund of the fee charged with no driver compensation, so driver_compensation_sgd is null.

No escalation is available to the driver. The fact POL-NS-23 turns on — that no call was placed — is not an inference drawn from absent evidence; it is the affirmative content of two COMPLETE artifacts carrying weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05052's empty in_app_calls array and EV-CHAT-05052's call-free log). The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05052-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, but neither POL-NS-23 nor POL-NS-21 requires a traffic advisory, so POL-GEN-26's route to escalation for an unestablishable fact is not open here.

The driver cancelled at 19:37:20 — 380 s after arrival and 75 s after the platform's own wait timer expired at 19:36:05 — so the free-wait precondition for cancelling as a rider no-show is satisfied on the trip record with time to spare.

The free-wait condition (POL-NS-21) and the fee amount (POL-NS-22: 5.00 SGD, matching policy) are satisfied. But POL-NS-23 adds a separate, cumulative precondition on any no-show cancellation: before cancelling, the driver must have sent at least one in-app message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider. Only the message half is met — two in-app messages at 19:31:30 and 19:34:10 — while trip_record.in_app_calls is empty (call_count 0) and the platform chat log of three entries contains no voice-call entry. Both artifacts are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so this is affirmative evidence of a missing call, not an inference from absent evidence. The driver’s own statement ('I sent 2 messages and waited more than 5 minutes. Passenger never reply.') concedes the message half only. POL-NS-23 provides that if either element is missing the fee is voided and the rider is not charged.

Because the rider filed (filed_by RIDER) and is owed the whole contested amount, the ruling is FULL_REFUND with amount_sgd 5.00 and driver_compensation_sgd null.

The driver’s claims are answered and outweighed. The corroborated arrival and the fully served free wait do not rescue the fee: they satisfy POL-NS-21, which governs how long to wait, not whether the charge is licensed. The plea for DRIVER_COMPENSATION under POL-NS-22 fails because that clause applies only 'where the fee stands', and it does not stand once the POL-NS-23 contact precondition failed; for the same reason the party-relative NO_ACTION argument (that the present payment state should simply remain) cannot hold — the fee is void, not standing. POL-NS-24 (driver no-show) does not open either: the driver did arrive, and an on-demand trip carries no scheduled time to measure a deadline against. The claim that the rider’s 'in the lift' excuse is contradicted by the read receipts (19:31:40 and 19:34:23, before cancellation; her reply at 19:38:05, after it) is accepted as fact but changes nothing — POL-NS-23’s contact obligation is unconditional and does not turn on the rider's whereabouts or responsiveness.

No referral arises. The fee charged is exactly the policy 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22’s amount-check referral does not fire; POL-NS-24’s goodwill credit does not fire because the driver did arrive; and the POL-NS-25 repeat-count field (rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d) is not present on this profile. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05052-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and is not needed by either POL-NS-21 or POL-NS-23, so POL-GEN-26 opens no escalation: the fact this case turns on — that no call was placed before cancellation — is established by complete, weight-1.0 evidence. Confidence rests on those complete artifacts (cap 1.0), and with a contested value of 5.00 SGD below POL-GEN-22’s first band, POL-NS-26 makes this AI ruling final.

ruling.explanation:
The rider filed this dispute, so the outcome is read from the rider's claim. What is at stake is the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee on the payments ledger (EV-FARE-05052: cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0).

The fee does not stand. POL-NS-23 (v2.1 section 2.3) provides that before a driver may cancel for a rider no-show he must BOTH have sent at least one in-app message AND have placed at least one in-app call to the rider, each before cancelled_at; if either is missing, the fee is voided and the rider is refunded in full with no driver compensation. On this record the trip record's in_app_calls array is empty and its derived contact_before_cancel block records call_count 0, and the chat log (EV-CHAT-05052) contains three in-app text entries and no voice-call entry. Both artifacts are COMPLETE at weight 1.00. The message half was met (MSG-05052-001 sent 19:31:30 and MSG-05052-002 sent 19:34:10, both before the 19:37:20 cancellation, both read by the rider), but the call half was not performed, and the clause is conjunctive. The driver's own statement concedes only two messages, and the driver's advocate candidly concedes the call limb is not evidenced; the charge cannot rest on the contact limb. The fee is therefore voided: the whole 5.00 SGD is returned to the rider and driver_compensation_sgd is null.

The driver's remaining points are accurate but do not save the charge. The arrival was corroborated independently of his app button: the nearest GPS fix sits 2.73 m from the Block 512 pickup coordinate with reported accuracy 5 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD-zone arrival radius and the 120 s window (EV-GPS-05052, EV-TRIP-05052; arrival_check corroborated = true). The free wait was served in full: this was an on-demand booking with scheduled_at null, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s wait ran from arrival at 19:31:00 and expired at 19:36:00, while the driver cancelled at 19:37:20, 380 s after arrival. But POL-NS-21 governs only how long the driver must wait; it does not license the charge. POL-NS-23 imposes a separate, cumulative precondition on the same cancellation, and that precondition fails. The driver's argument that the record's corroborated arrival, served wait and correct 5.00 SGD amount support DRIVER_COMPENSATION is accepted as far as the amount fact goes (fee_matches_policy = true) but rejected as an outcome, because the fee must first survive POL-NS-23, and it does not. The rider's statement that she was 'in the lift with no signal' is indeed not borne out by the chat log, which shows both driver messages delivered and read (read_at 19:31:40 and 19:34:23), but that is beside the point: POL-NS-23 does not turn on where the rider was or whether she replied, so this finding does not weaken her claim. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05052-01, weight 0.00, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and changes nothing, and POL-NS-24's driver-no-show route does not open here because an on-demand trip has no scheduled time and the driver in fact arrived and waited.

No referral fires. The record charged exactly the 5.00 SGD policy amount, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not apply. POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not open: it needs the driver to have failed to arrive by a scheduled time plus five minutes, and there is none. POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag does not apply: the profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d of 3 or more (no_show_disputes_30d is 0), and in any event the fee does not stand. The dispute is below 10.00 SGD and neither party carries a fraud flag, so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final at any confidence; POL-GEN-26 does not escalate, because the decisive fact — that no call was placed — is the affirmative content of two complete records at weight 1.00, not an inference from missing evidence.

Confidence: the fact that decides this case (no in-app call before cancellation) is carried by EV-TRIP-05052 and EV-CHAT-05052, each at weight 1.00, so the cap is 1.00; I rule at 0.95. 5.00 SGD is returned to the rider.

ruling.explanation:
This dispute is about the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-05052 (cancelled 8 Aug 2026, 19:37:20). The rider filed, so the outcome is read from the rider's claim against the record, and the rider is owed the whole contested amount.

The driver did serve the free wait. He marked arrival at 19:31:00, and the GPS trace corroborates it (nearest fix 2.73 m from the Block 512 pickup point, with a reported accuracy of 5 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius). This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from arrival and expired at 19:36:00; the driver cancelled at 19:37:20, after it expired. The fee charged was exactly 5.00 SGD, matching the policy amount (POL-NS-22).

But the fee cannot stand. POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for a no-show, to have BOTH sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider, both before cancelled_at. The message half is met — two in-app messages at 19:31:30 and 19:34:10, both before the 19:37:20 cancellation, both delivered and read. The call half is not: the trip record's in_app_calls array is empty and the chat log's three entries are all in-app text with no voice-call entry. Both are complete weight-1.0 artifacts, and nothing else carries a call for this trip (the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05052-01 is missing, weight 0.0, but no clause here requires one). Where either element is missing, POL-NS-23 voids the fee and the rider is not charged: a full refund of the fee with no driver compensation.

I have weighed the driver's arguments and they do not change the result. DRIVER_COMPENSATION under POL-NS-22, and the NO_ACTION argument under POL-GEN-03, both presuppose that the fee stands; it does not, because POL-NS-23's cumulative contact precondition was not performed, so there is nothing to transfer to the driver and nothing for the present state to preserve. The driver's point that the rider read both messages during the wait (read receipts 19:31:40 and 19:34:23) is accepted as true, but the contact obligation is unconditional and does not turn on the rider's whereabouts — it is precisely because a rider may be momentarily unreachable that the clause requires a call as well as a message. The rider's alternative ground of driver no-show under POL-NS-24 does not arise: this was an on-demand trip and the driver did arrive and wait.

No escalation applies. The facts the rules need — that the driver arrived, waited the full free period, sent messages and placed no call — are all affirmatively established on complete weight-1.0 artifacts, so POL-GEN-26's route to escalation for a fact the record cannot establish is not open. There is no safety flag and no fraud flag, and the contested value of 5.00 SGD is below 10.00 SGD, where POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 make the AI ruling final at any confidence.

No referral is produced. The fee charged was exactly the policy 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire; the rider's no-show counter is not present on the profile and this trip's fee does not stand, so POL-NS-25's repeat no-show referral does not fire; and no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit arises, as the driver was not a no-show and did attempt contact.

Outcome: 5.00 SGD is refunded to the rider (amount_sgd 5.00); the driver receives no compensation (driver_compensation_sgd null).

ledger.claim: POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for no-show, to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider. The trip record's in_app_calls array is empty and the derived contact_before_cancel block reports call_count of 0, while the platform chat log's three entries include no voice-call entry. The call limb is therefore missing, and the clause provides that if either element is missing the fee is voided and the rider is not charged.

The driver's own statement — 'I sent 2 messages and waited more than 5 minutes. Passenger never reply.' — concedes the position: messages alone are not the obligation. The two messages (MSG-05052-001 at 19:31:30 and MSG-05052-002 at 19:34:10, both before cancelled_at at 19:37:20) satisfy only the first limb of POL-NS-23. The clause is conjunctive and its second limb is unperformed, so the contact obligation is not met and the fee fails.

Even on the driver's best possible version of the timing — arrived_at 19:31:00, free-wait expiry 19:36:00, cancelled_at 19:37:20, elapsed 380.0 seconds — only the free-wait rule in POL-NS-21 is satisfied. POL-NS-21 governs how long the driver must wait; it does not license the charge. POL-NS-23 imposes a separate, cumulative precondition on the very same cancellation, and because that precondition is unmet no no-show fee may be charged at all.

The rider's explanation that he was in a lift with no signal is not corroborated by the record — the chat log shows both driver messages were delivered and read (read_at 19:31:40 and 19:34:23). That does not weaken the claim, and the rider should not have to rely on it: POL-NS-23's contact obligation is unconditional and does not turn on where the rider was or whether he responded. A rider momentarily out of signal is precisely the situation the policy addresses by requiring a call as well as a message, and the entitlement to a refund is independent of the rider's whereabouts.

The rider filed this dispute (filed_by RIDER) and the payments ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 5.00 SGD and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 — nothing has been returned. Under POL-GEN-03 a rider-side filing that is entirely right produces FULL_REFUND of the whole contested amount, and POL-NS-23 fixes the consequence of a voided fee as refund of the fee charged with no driver compensation, so driver_compensation_sgd is null.

No escalation is available to the driver. The fact POL-NS-23 turns on — that no call was placed — is not an inference drawn from absent evidence; it is the affirmative content of two COMPLETE artifacts carrying weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05052's empty in_app_calls array and EV-CHAT-05052's call-free log). The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05052-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, but neither POL-NS-23 nor POL-NS-21 requires a traffic advisory, so POL-GEN-26's route to escalation for an unestablishable fact is not open here.

The driver's arrival at the pickup is corroborated by the GPS trace and does not rest on his app button alone: the nearest fix is 2.73 m from the Block 512, Bedok North Street 3 pickup coordinate, with a reported accuracy of 5 m, which is inside the STANDARD zone arrival radius of 50 m and inside the 120 s corroboration window, and the arrival check on this trace returns corroborated = true. Both EV-TRIP-05052 and EV-GPS-05052 are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so this finding is unimpaired.

The free wait was served in full. This was an on-demand booking with scheduled_at null, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival at 19:31:00 and expires at 19:36:00. The driver cancelled at 19:37:20 — 380 s after arrival and 75 s after the platform's own wait timer expired at 19:36:05 — so the free-wait precondition for cancelling as a rider no-show is satisfied on the trip record with time to spare.

Nothing on this record puts the wait at the driver's door. He was assigned at 19:23:05, began navigating at 19:23:11 and arrived at 19:31:00, and the only external artifact for this trip — the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05052-01 — is MISSING, issues [MISSING_ARTIFACT], weight 0.0, so no advisory is on file and there is no evidenced delay to excuse the rider's absence.

The amount charged is exactly the policy amount. The payments ledger carries a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0, and fee_matches_policy = true. Under POL-NS-22 that fee is payable to the driver as compensation for time and fuel where it stands, so on the substantive no-show test the record supports DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both at 5.00.

The outcome must be read off this filer. The rider filed (filed_by RIDER) and the 5.00 SGD is still charged with no refund issued, so under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and preserves the present payment state — it leaves the fee with the driver and records that the rider's claim as filed is not supported. NO_ACTION never means restoring a charge; here it is simply the fee standing.

The rider's excuse for not coming down — that she was 'in the lift with no signal' — is contradicted by the chat log. The platform delivered both driver messages and records the rider reading them at 19:31:40 and 19:34:23, both before the 19:37:20 cancellation; her only reply came at 19:38:05, 45 s after the trip was cancelled. She therefore had connectivity during the free wait, was alerted that the driver was at the void deck, and chose not to come down until after the driver had waited the full period and left.

The rider's other route to a refund, driver no-show under POL-NS-24, does not open on this record: this is an on-demand trip with no scheduled pickup time, so there is no 'scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes' to measure the driver against, and in any event the driver arrived 7 min 55 s after being assigned and waited the full free period.

Candidly, the contact obligation is the one limb the record does not carry in full. Under POL-NS-23 the driver must have sent at least one in-app message AND placed at least one in-app call before cancelled_at. The message half is met and is admitted on both sides — two in-app messages at 19:31:30 and 19:34:10, both before cancellation, both read by the rider — but trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and the chat log's three contiguous entries are all in-app text with no voice-call entry, so the call half is not evidenced on EV-TRIP-05052 or EV-CHAT-05052. The driver does not overstate the point: his case for keeping the fee rests on the corroborated arrival, the served free wait and the correct 5.00 SGD fee, not on the contact limb.
